subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` become a pre-handshake rejection policy for every Origin-bearing Gateway WebSocket client, or remain limited to traffic that is classified as Control UI under the current admission contract?
rationale: This is a security-boundary and compatibility choice: the new hook runs before the existing protocol/authentication path can establish client intent, so source inspection cannot determine whether rejecting all Origin-bearing clients is the intended product contract.

options.title: Keep the current Control UI scope
options.body: Add a pre-handshake predicate that preserves the current client-aware admission boundary and prove direct, proxied, and non-UI client behavior.

options.title: Adopt all-Origin pre-handshake enforcement
options.body: Explicitly document the broader Gateway client contract, assess affected protocol clients, and add upgrade and live-proxy proof before merging.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the existing post-handshake check until a safe pre-handshake client-classification seam is agreed.

recommendation.title: Keep the current Control UI scope
recommendation.body: Add a pre-handshake predicate that preserves the current client-aware admission boundary and prove direct, proxied, and non-UI client behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work on the reused origin-check helper makes them the closest identifiable history-based routing candidate for this policy decision.
